question: Can a promptable segmentation task, model and model-in-the-loop data engine produce a foundation model for image segmentation that transfers zero-shot to new distributions and tasks?
hypothesis: A model pre-trained on a promptable segmentation task over a very large, diverse mask dataset will generalise zero-shot to new tasks via prompt engineering.
contributions: A three-stage data engine and the SA-1B dataset of 1.1B masks on 11M images (Sec 4-5)
Responsible AI analysis and zero-shot transfer evaluation on five tasks (Sec 6-7)

method.summary: SAM is an MAE-pretrained ViT-H image encoder, a prompt encoder (points, boxes, masks, CLIP text) and a two-layer lightweight transformer mask decoder predicting 3 ambiguity-aware masks plus IoU scores. It is trained on SA-1B, whose masks were produced by a three-stage data engine (assisted-manual, semi-automatic, fully automatic), then evaluated zero-shot on point-to-mask (23 datasets), edge detection, object proposals, instance segmentation and text-to-mask.
method.task: promptable image segmentation (pre-training) with zero-shot transfer by prompting

datasets.name: SA-1B
datasets.size: 11M images, 1.1B masks (1129M); ~100 masks/image; images avg 3300x4950 px, released downsampled to shortest side 1500
datasets.split: ~2k random images withheld for testing; default training uses only the automatic masks
datasets.source: Images licensed from a photo provider; masks generated by SAM; faces and license plates blurred; research licence
datasets.preprocessing: Masks covering over 90% of the image discarded for training; automatic masks drop those covering >=95%, small components/holes <100 px removed

datasets.name: Data engine stage 1 (assisted-manual)
datasets.source: Professional annotators (130, Kenya) with SAM tool; not released

datasets.name: Data engine stage 2 (semi-automatic)
datasets.source: Annotators plus box detector masks; not released

datasets.name: 23-dataset zero-shot point suite
datasets.size: datasets with >15k masks subsampled to ~10k masks
datasets.source: 23 public datasets (ADE20K, BBBC038v1, Cityscapes, DOORS, DRAM, EgoHOS, GTEA, Hypersim, IBD, iShape, LVIS, NDD20, NDISPark, OVIS, PPDLS, Plittersdorf, STREETS, TimberSeg, TrashCan, VISOR, WoodScape, PIDRay, ZeroWaste-f)

datasets.name: BSDS500
datasets.source: Martin et al. / Arbelaez et al.

datasets.name: MIAP + Open Images
datasets.source: MIAP annotations for Open Images; proprietary skin-tone dataset (Fitzpatrick)
datasets.preprocessing: person masks matched to MIAP boxes within 1% margin

models.name: SAM (ViT-H)
models.architecture: ViT-H/16 image encoder (14x14 windowed attention, 4 global blocks, 1024x1024 input, 64x64x256 embedding) + prompt encoder + 2-layer transformer mask decoder

other.outputs: 3 masks + IoU score (4th token for multi-prompt)
other.mask_prompt: 4x lower res, 2 convs ch 4 and 16, 1x1 conv to 256

training.objective: Mask loss 20:1 focal:dice, min-over-3-masks backprop; IoU head MSE with scale 1.0; no auxiliary deep supervision; prompts simulated interactively over 11 iterations (1 initial point-or-box with equal probability, 8 sampled points, 2 no-new-info iterations)
training.lr_schedule: step decay: /10 at 60k iterations and again at 86666
training.regularisation: drop path 0.4; layer-wise lr decay 0.8; no data augmentation; up to 64 sampled masks per GPU

other.vitb_vitl: 180k iterations, batch 128 on 128 GPUs; lr 8e-4/4e-4, ld 0.6/0.8, wd 0.1, dp 0.6/0.4 for ViT-B/L
other.auto_mask_model: trained on manual+semi-auto data only, 177656 iterations, large-scale jitter [0.1,2.0], point+mask prompts only, 4 points/mask, 3-layer decoder
other.text_to_mask: masks of first two stages, area>=100^2, large-scale jitter, 120k iterations, batch 128, CLIP image embeddings of crops as first prompt
other.box_noise: std 10% of box side, max 20 px

inference.decoding: point-to-mask: most confident of 3 masks (default); center point = max of interior distance transform
inference.samples: single deterministic run per item; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: geometric prompts (points, boxes, masks) and CLIP text embedding

parameters.auto_mask_grid: 32x32 points on full image plus 20 zoomed crops (2x2 windows with 16x16 grid, 4x4 windows with 8x8 grid)
parameters.edge_grid: 16x16 points, 768 masks, no IoU/stability filter, Sobel + edge NMS
parameters.proposal_grid: 64x64, NMS 0.9, ~900 masks/image, top 1000 by mean of confidence and stability
parameters.instance_seg: ViTDet-H boxes as prompts plus one refinement iteration with best mask + box

other.eval_points: N in {1,2,3,5,9}; first point farthest from boundary, later points farthest from error region

metrics.name: mIoU
metrics.definition: per-mask IoU averaged within dataset, then averaged over 23 datasets

metrics.name: mask AR@1000
metrics.definition: average recall at 1000 proposals on LVIS v1, also by size and frequency

metrics.name: mask AP
metrics.definition: instance segmentation AP on COCO and LVIS v1

eval.protocol: Human study: 30 annotators, one annotator per job, 1000 masks per dataset per model, 7 datasets for points, LVIS v1 1000 boxes for instance seg; masks <24^2 px excluded; paired t-test and paired bootstrap (10k samples) 99% CI, all significant; pilot of 5 raters per job gave mean sd 0.83. Fairness: 95% confidence intervals.

limits: Can miss fine structures, hallucinate small disconnected components, and boundaries are less crisp than zoom-in methods.
Dedicated interactive methods expected to beat SAM with many points; not optimised for high IoU regime.
Overall performance is not real-time with the heavy image encoder (only prompt+decoder is).
Text-to-mask is exploratory and not entirely robust; no simple prompts for semantic or panoptic segmentation.
Domain-specific tools expected to beat SAM in their domains.
Africa, Latin America and low-income countries are underrepresented in SA-1B; clothing segmentation shows a gender-presentation gap at 1 point.
Single-run numbers; no seeds reported for training; compute for data-engine retrainings not stated.
